title: FDA RSABE, fully replicate, CVwR 40%, ratio 0.90, n=24

oracle.arguments: power.RSABE(CV=0.40, theta0=0.90, n=24, design="2x2x4", regulator=reg_const("USER", r_const=log(1.25)/0.25, CVswitch=0, CVcap=Inf, pe_constr=TRUE), details=TRUE, nsims=1e5)
oracle.method_note: PowerTOST computes empirical power by simulating nsims studies from the distributional properties of the deciding statistics. be-stats analyses datasets, so the Python side simulates studies and applies the be-stats criterion to each. Two Monte Carlo estimates of one probability, compared at the only layer both expose.
oracle.regulatory_setting_note: FDA's r_const and the unchanged "fda" criterion, with CVswitch=0 so PowerTOST's p(BE-sABEc) is the scaled criterion ALONE. See VAL-FDA-HVD-001. At CVwR 0.40 only about 6 percent of studies fall below the FDA switch, so this case agreed under the previous setting too - which is why the mismatch showed only at the boundary.

comparisons.tolerance_basis: DERIVED, and independent of the answer. Both sides estimate the same probability by simulation, so the difference between them has standard deviation sqrt(p(1-p)(1/n_python + 1/n_R)). Evaluated at the WORST CASE p = 0.5, which maximises p(1-p), and taken at four standard deviations: 4 * sqrt(0.25 * (1/20000 + 1/100000)) = 0.01549. Using worst-case p rather than the observed p means the tolerance was fixed before either side was run. Wide enough that two agreeing implementations pass essentially always; narrow enough that a procedural difference of more than about 1.5 percentage points fails.

DERIVED, one-sided. The R side computes this in CLOSED FORM: sWR^2 * dfRR / sigma^2_wR is chi-square on dfRR = n - 2 = 22 degrees of freedom under the model both sides simulate. Only the Python side carries sampling error, so the tolerance is 4 * sqrt(0.25/20000) = 0.01414 at worst-case p = 0.5. Fixed before the run.

not_cross_checkable: The overall p(BE), and the mixed procedure generally. PowerTOST decides below the switch by a TOST on the same intra-subject contrast; FDA specifies Appendix C's mixed model, which be-stats records and refuses to approximate (see replicate_abe.py). Neither PowerTOST's convention nor be-stats' silence can validate the other.

The intermediate Howe quantities x, bound_x, y and bound_y. PowerTOST does not expose them for a dataset; it exposes only the probability that the criterion passed. They are checked instead against the FDA SAS in the tier-1A case FDA-HVD-RSABE-CRITERION-001.

sWR and the treatment contrast for any individual study. PowerTOST analyses no dataset, so there is nothing to compare them with. This is not a gap that can be closed by choosing different arguments: PowerTOST 1.5-7 exposes no dataset-level entry point for the FDA scaled procedures at all.
notes: A comfortably highly variable scenario where reference scaling is doing real work and few simulated studies fall below the switch.
